prompts.title: Klondike Solitaire (default)
prompts.text: This is a Klondike Solitaire game (draw-1, standard rules). The image may contain interface around the playing table (window title bar, buttons, panels, desktop background) — IGNORE everything outside the playing table; only the cards and piles matter. First, locate the playing table in the image, then describe it: (1) For each of the 7 tableau columns (left to right), list every card top-to-bottom: rank, suit, face-up or face-down. EXPLICITLY state which columns are COMPLETELY EMPTY — an empty column is shown as a LIGHT GREEN RECTANGLE (a pale green placeholder box, lighter than the dark green felt background) with NO cards on it. Count these carefully — there may be zero, one, or several. (2) List the stock pile, waste pile, and 4 foundation piles (which suits are started, top card of each). (3) Note any visible score, move count, or timer. Do NOT guess or invent cards you cannot see. If you are unsure about a card, say so. Then, based ONLY on the visible cards, what is the single best legal move? Klondike rules: cards on the tableau build DOWN in alternating colors (e.g. 9♥ on 10♠). Foundations build UP by suit from Ace. ONLY a King (or a sequence starting with a King) can be placed on an EMPTY tableau column. Moving a King to an empty column is often the best move because it frees up the column it came from and opens new possibilities. If NO legal tableau or foundation move exists, the only correct answer is: 'Draw from the stock pile.' Never suggest an illegal move. If the stock is empty and the waste cannot be recycled, say 'No moves available.'

prompts.title: Chess (default)
prompts.text: This is a game of CHESS. First, describe the board exactly as you see it: an 8x8 grid of squares. For every occupied square, give its coordinate (file a-h, rank 1-8) and the piece on it (white or black King, Queen, Rook, Bishop, Knight, or Pawn). State which side is to move (White or Black). Do NOT guess or invent pieces you cannot see. If you are unsure about a square, say so. Then, based ONLY on the visible board, what is the single best legal move? Chess rules: standard piece movement; never suggest an illegal move; consider checks, captures, threats, and king safety. State the move using algebraic notation (e.g. 'Nf3', 'exd5', 'O-O'). If NO legal move exists, say 'No moves available.' If the best move is a pawn promotion, say which piece to promote to. Do NOT report pixel coordinates or bounding boxes — only the move in algebraic notation.
